messages:
maya: hitting a big throughput drop on prod-dedicated-pool-a ~15:30 UTC. P50s up 3x and several workers restarting. seeing repeated GPU OOMs and a flurry of slab evictions in the allocator logs.
jun: can you paste the allocator/log lines?
maya: paste from node-12 (cropped):
```
[15:29:51] allocator: slab_evict: slab=kv_cache size=48MB -> evicted 4 pages
[15:29:51] runtime: kernel_select: chosen=fast-attn-v2 fallback=matmul-compat reason=mem-frag
[15:29:52] worker[72]: OOM signal, trying graceful shutdown
[15:29:52] allocator: frag_stats: free_contiguous=12MB, total_free=64MB, largest_free_chunk=8MB
[15:29:52] runtime: batch_coalescer: flushed 3 batches due to kernel_fallback
[15:29:53] worker[72]: restart requested by supervisor
```
arjun: that kernel_select log stands out — we changed the multi-kernel fallback thresholds in last week's rollout. if runtime is choosing fallback for many requests, kernel path becomes larger memory footprint -> OOM cascade.
tori: noisy tenant pattern? any spike in sequence length distribution?
maya: seq len distribution shifted — a small client started sending a lot of long-history chat, median seqlen for node-12 went 256->1024 for a short window. KV cache fragmentation increased due to many prefix cache writes.
jun: ran pprof on node-12 earlier. top heatmap shows kv_cache allocs concentrated in bin 512-1024. attaching snippet:
```
(pprof) top10
  34.2% runtime.kv_cache.write
  22.1% runtime.attn_kernel.allocate_workspace
  12.5% runtime.batch_coalescer.coalesce
  8.7% runtime.kernel_router.route_with_constraints
```
```
(pprof) memlive
  kv_cache: 120MB live (active pages scattered)
  slab_allocator: total 512MB, fragmented 46%
```
ops: deploy-bot shows a canary kernel heuristic update at 2000120700 with flag rollout=30% -> suspects.
arjun: yep, that matches. the heuristic relaxed fallback guard to reduce latency for small batches — but in mixed seqlen workloads it increases fallback churn.
maya: what triggered the worker restarts vs OOM kills? logs show graceful restart path then rapid rejoin and another OOM. repeat pattern for ~20 workers in the node set.
jun: hypothesis: kernel fallback causes slower kernel (higher workspace) which prevents timely KV eviction, slab allocator falls into fragmentation -> subsequent requests can't grab contiguous chunk -> OOM. restarts free memory but allocation pattern repeats.
tori: can we mitigate quickly? options: 1) rollback kernel heuristic flag 2) increase per-worker reserved contiguous slab 3) temporarily throttle long-seq tenant 4) scale up pool capacity
arjun: immediate: flip rollout->0% to stop more hosts selecting new heuristic. also enable aggressive KV prefix coalescing to reduce fragmentation.
maya: doing flag flip now: `/admin/flags set runtime.kernel_relax_rollout 0`
deploy-bot: flag runtime.kernel_relax_rollout set to 0 by maya at 15:36:12 UTC
sre-bot: alert: started bulk slab compaction on node-12..node-15 (background sweep enabled)
jun: good. also push a short-term guard in runtime: if fragile fragmentation>40% prefer older kernel even for small batches. that'll avoid oscillation.
arjun: agree. I'll open a small PR for kernel_router: add frag_ratio check before picking fallback. keeps fallback disabled when fragmentation high.
tori: for the tenant that caused seqlen spike, can we QPS-throttle them to reduce immediate pressure?
maya: throttling applied via rate-limiter rule rl-tenant-17 at 15:39.
ops: observed p50 back down to 1.1x baseline and no OOMs in last 4 mins after actions.
jun: follow-ups: 1) revert rollout permanently until we have perf test covering mixed seqlen; 2) add workload-eval to e2e perf harness with long-chat traces; 3) telemetry: emit kernel_select_reason + frag_ratio in trace spans for next 7 days.
arjun: PR #2345 opened with frag_ratio guard and unit tests. planning hotfix release to canary tomorrow if tests pass.
maya: thanks everyone. adding postmortem slot for tomorrow 11:00 to capture root cause and propose changes to batching heuristics and kv cache compaction policy.
tori: adding to calendar.
sre-bot: incident resolved: throughput normalized, workers stable. closing page. :white_check_mark:
